title: C# Question & Answers - Generic Methods
sourceFile: Generic Methods - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on generic methods in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: In the following C# code, which statement is NOT correct?

options.text: Class MyContainer requires that its type argument must implement IComparable interface
There are multiple constraints on the type argument of MyContainer class
Class MyContainer requires that its type argument must be a reference type
The compiler will report an error because the syntax is invalid

questions.explanation: The syntax is perfectly valid. The 'where' clause correctly specifies that T must be a class (reference type) and must implement the IComparable interface.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is valid about generics in .NET?

options.text: Generics are highly useful for creating type-safe collection classes
Generic delegates are not allowed in C#
Generics is a runtime-only feature and not a language feature

questions.explanation: Generics allow you to write a class or method that can work with any data type while providing full type safety and performance benefits, especially in collections like List<T>.

questions.question: What is the output of the following C# code?

questions.explanation: 'Generic' is not a reserved keyword in C#, so it can be used as a class name. The code correctly instantiates a generic class with string and prints the field.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid statement regarding generic methods in C#?

options.text: All methods inside a generic class must be generic
Generic methods must define at least one type parameter in angle brackets
Only static methods can be generic

questions.explanation: A generic method is defined by specifying a type parameter list in angle brackets after the method name, such as 'void MyMethod<T>(T arg)'.

questions.question: In the following C# code, what does the constraint 'where T : IComparable' enforce?
questions.code: public class MyContainer<T> where T : IComparable { }

options.text: T must implement the IComparable interface
There are multiple constraints on T

questions.explanation: The 'where T : IComparable' constraint ensures that only types that implement the IComparable interface can be used as type arguments for T.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid generic collection class in the System.Collections.Generic namespace?
questions.explanation: SortedDictionary<TKey, TValue> is a generic collection. ArrayList and Hashtable are non-generic collections located in System.Collections.

questions.explanation: Generic classes create a specialized version of the class for each type used. Both instances work independently and print their respective values: 'C++' and '20'.
